snippet.title: Seasons of Books and Keys - Official Announcement Trailer
snippet.description:
Wishlist on Steam:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4972460/_/?utm_source=shueishagames&utm_campaign=organic&utm_medium=youtube

Honobu Yonezawa's bestselling mystery novel Seasons of Books and Keys is becoming a game. This winter, a drama-like adventure that draws you into a bittersweet mystery, taken on by two high schoolers on the library committee, arrives on Nintendo Switch and Steam.

Take in each mystery the two library-committee boys face: reach for it with your eyes, listen for it with your ears, and unravel it with your own hands, as if turning the pages of a book. It is a bittersweet coming-of-age mystery adventure rooted in the everyday, one you sink into with all five senses, the way you would watch a single drama.

The game adapts the novel Seasons of Books and Keys (Shueisha Bunko) by Honobu Yonezawa, the author behind Hyouka, the Shoushimin Series, and The Samurai and the Prisoner. Its full scenario is told with rich color illustration and complete voice acting, and it adds an all-new episode, "Used Kitan," written for this release by Yonezawa himself. The main character designs are newly drawn by Yoko Tanji, the illustrator who created the original novel's key visual.

▶ Characters

Jiro Horikawa (voiced by Kazuki Ura)
People are always bringing him their problems, and he tends to trust them, though he has a sharp eye for detail. Ever since he started spending time with Matsukura, he keeps getting pulled into strange situations.

Shimon Matsukura (voiced by Yuichirou Umehara)
Sardonic, and older than his years in the way he thinks. Tall and good-looking, he stands out. Ever since he started spending time with Horikawa, he keeps getting pulled into strange situations.

▶ What is a drama-like adventure?

Drama-like adventure is the genre built for this title, fusing the experience of reading a story with the experience of watching one. You take it in with your eyes, listen with your ears, and operate with your fingers, feeling the narrative through every sense and sinking into it as if you were watching a single drama.

The lingering resonance of the printed page stays intact, while the story gains the immediacy of film. The aim is an experience where even the smallest shifts in a character's heart come through in a way you can feel with all five senses.

▶ Drama-like adventure Seasons of Books and Keys overview
